frozen_before: any model in this study was fitted or scored; the 2026 season outcomes were never read by the author of this file
market_family: NFL full-game lines: winner (KXNFLGAME), point spread (KXNFLSPREAD), total points (KXNFLTOTAL)
prediction_cutoff: scheduled kickoff; every feature uses games dated strictly before the game date (dataset manifest)
labels: final score from the dataset for model fitting and point metrics; Kalshi OFFICIAL results (vault snapshot-20261116) for every contract-level probability score
baseline: record_strength = walk-forward ridge on the certified season-record inputs only (Pythagorean expectation, win pct, luck); climatology = expanding league mean (home-field constant)

multiple_testing: Holm across all 22 hypotheses on the TEST seasons (alpha 0.05); DEMONSTRATED also needs both chronological halves > 0, every leave-one-season-out > 0 and a season-block CI > 0
primary_questions: Does the full certified-input model beat the record-strength reference and climatology out of sample?
How far is the sports-only model from the sportsbook closing line (MAE, squared error, side hit rate)?
Is the model's win probability calibrated, and how does its Brier score compare with the de-vigged closing moneyline?
On real Kalshi contracts with official results, how do model probabilities score against a closing-line-derived benchmark?
not_claimed: no betting value: no executable Kalshi price, liquidity or fee evidence is used; closing sportsbook lines have no quote timestamp
holdout_rule: 2026 outcomes are blanked before any fit unless --holdout; holdout.json is written once and is tied to this file's hash
